name: Basal Ganglia Circuitry and Movement Disorders

reference.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students / Kandel's Principles of Neural Science
clinicalPearls: Corpus striatum consists of caudate nucleus and lentiform nucleus (putamen and globus pallidus)
Direct pathway (D1 receptors) disinhibits thalamus via striatal inhibition of GPi, facilitating intended voluntary movements
Indirect pathway (D2 receptors) excites GPi via subthalamic nucleus, suppressing unwanted motor programmes
Parkinson disease: loss of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra pars compacta reduces direct pathway activity and overactivates indirect pathway
Hemiballismus: lacunar infarction of contralateral subthalamic nucleus causes violent involuntary flinging limb movements
reference.pathophysiology: The basal ganglia modulate motor cortical output through balanced direct (facilitatory) and indirect (inhibitory) loops. In Parkinson disease, alpha-synuclein Lewy body pathology destroys nigrostriatal dopamine projections, shifting the balance toward profound indirect pathway inhibition, causing bradykinesia, resting tremor and cogwheel rigidity. In Huntington disease, striatal GABA/enkephalin neuron loss disinhibits movement, causing chorea.
additionalInvestigations: Dopamine transporter SPECT (DaTscan) demonstrating asymmetric striatal uptake loss in Parkinsonism
Genetic testing for Huntington disease (CAG trinucleotide repeats in HTT gene >36)
Brain MRI showing caudate atrophy (box-car ventricles) in Huntington chorea
